title: Burned Guest Log
warm:
Rhea burned a page of the guest log in the desk grate and the smell turned Crownspire's lobby into a crime of paper. Soft interview broke. Detective Imani Brooks's face went from mercy to inventory. [player_name] tasted ash on recycled air and understood homicide interest did not need a body when buildings started editing themselves. Vivienne's marks—weekly to monthly to gone—had just lost a sibling sentence to fire. Four fates still open; one piece of memory not.

"That was not on my order," [player_name] said, early thirties, soft alibi cracking in public. Nolan Greer stood too close; Marcus Pell stood too far; Rhea's hands shook once and then remembered employment.

Brooks did not raise her voice. "Obstruction has a scent. Soft neighbors collect it. Mr. Greer's holding collects it. Concierges collect it when money walks by. Someone will own this ash."

Elevator chime. Wind sheer. Unused perfume waited upstairs like innocence that had never been true. Black car at the curb as if summoned by panic. [player_name] felt trust versus complicity put on her coat without asking.

Nolan's cufflinks clicked. "We open my locked drawer upstairs—full cooperation under watch—or we plan the hangar raid with or against Pell before Brooks turns ash into a warrant shaped like your door."

Pell's mild voice arrived late: "Against me is theater. With me is survival. Drawer is romantic confession wearing wood. Choose before the detective invents your preference."

[player_name] looked at burned grate, badge, Nolan's telling wrist, Rhea's carefully blank eyes. Soft interview was dead. Soft alibi was only mostly dead. She had to pick whether full coop meant unlocking Nolan's silence—or raid planning meant taking the burn outside Crownspire's curb.

She catalogued what Crownspire still offered as soft machinery: elevator chime late at night, wine glass ring on marble, Vivienne's unused perfume in a bath she should not know, black car idling at the curb, Brooks's badge flash in the lobby, Nolan's cufflinks clicking when he lied, Rhea's slate with thinning marks, wind sheer against floor-to-ceiling glass. Anchors rotated through the hour without stacking into elegant absolutes. Dialogue had already carried the subtext; the anchors only kept score. Hope and dread shared every doorway. Vivienne's willing leave, paid vanish, death, or staging remained L10-open on purpose—Layer 5 only allowed homicide interest to rise, never a settled corpse to end the wanting or the dread. [player_name] felt the soft alibi's remaining give and understood consequence would spend it either way.

Burned guest log ash settled on Crownspire's performance of elegance like a dare. Concierges were not supposed to edit memory with fire; money was supposed to edit memory with NDAs. Rhea had chosen the cheaper, louder tool. Brooks would never forget the smell. [player_name] would never forget Nolan's face when soft interview cracked—charm banking, calculation rising, cufflinks loud. Full coop drawer meant opening silent-partner teeth that might rhyme with Vivienne without confirming her. Hangar raid planning meant converting ash panic into route and timing with or against Pell's mild poison. Soft alibi had to pick a next machine.
hot:
Ash on the air made [player_name] wet with adrenaline she refused to apologize for. Soft interview broken. Brooks's inventory gaze on her mouth. Nolan too close—rain-money cologne cutting ash—cufflink click traveling between her thighs like a guilty metronome. Early thirties. Across the hall. Vivienne contested. No body. Mid-want screaming anyway because fear and arousal had learned the same hallway.

"Drawer with him watching," she tasted, "or hangar raid with Pell's poison mildness." Both verbs lived low in her belly. Drawer meant unlocking while his body heat authored her. Raid meant planning violence-of-access without gore, hands shaking over maps instead of over her. Soft alibi pulse chose under badge light and burned paper scent.

Body-POV kept the through-line physical: pulse at throat, heat low in the belly, silk clinging, mid-want ending before climax because the next verb still owned the night. Nolan Greer only—mid-forties, finance and tech holding, brutal charm, rain-money cologne—romance lock unbroken. Crime stayed plot; intimacy stayed intimacy-forward, never gore-porn, never eroticizing absence as kink. Brooks's colder paper could press her skin; Vivienne's contested fate could press her ribs; neither turned sex into violence cosplay. [player_name] ached around unanswered questions the way Crownspire ached around a wife who might still be anywhere. Choosing hurt. Hurting meant the choice was real. Soft alibi had a pulse; Layer 5 made her feel every beat.

Ash-scent arousal was wrong and real—fight-or-flight chemistry translating into wet heat while Brooks inventoried her mouth. Nolan too close. Pell too mild. Rhea shaking then blank. Drawer-sex-adjacent confession energy versus raid-planning adrenaline: both substitutes for the hallway kiss they still had not finished. [player_name] chose knowing her body would try to fuck the verb into something simpler later.
